gen_risks.description: Delay or failure in passing the Children's Wellbeing and Schools Bill could compromise the statutory mandate requiring primary schools to provide free breakfast clubs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Engage closely with parliamentary stakeholders to track legislative progress and provide preliminary non-statutory guidance for voluntary school adoption.
gen_risks.evidence: Children's Wellbeing and Schools Bill will place a duty on state-funded schools with primary-aged children to offer a free breakfast club

gen_risks.description: Primary schools may lack sufficient physical dining or kitchen space to accommodate mandatory breakfast club provision for all pupils on roll.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy technical estate advisers to evaluate school premises and advise on spatial reconfiguration and flexible delivery options.
gen_risks.evidence: ...continuing contracts of technical estate advisers to test what schools can do to mitigate any space constraints.

gen_risks.description: Delays in developing the internal CRM minimum-viable product by November 2025 could disrupt the Cohort 1 expression of interest process and onboarding support.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement agile development sprints with dedicated internal resources and prepare fallback manual onboarding workflows.
gen_risks.evidence: ...develop a customer relationship management system internally, working towards a minimum-viable product from November 2025.

gen_risks.description: Simplified funding rates (£25 daily plus £1 per pupil) may fail to cover costs for schools facing high food inflation or non-standard staffing ratios.
gen_risks.mitigation: Monitor early rollout expenditure data closely and provide Section 14 grant adjustments or guidance on efficient food procurement.
gen_risks.evidence: Schools delivering their offer in-house, keeping food costs low, and staffing broadly in line with standard ratios were generally able to operate...

gen_risks.description: Closure of the National School Breakfast Programme in July 2026 could leave participating schools with a gap in provision before Cohort 2 starts in September 2026.
gen_risks.mitigation: Guarantee transition places for all current NSBP schools and streamline early application and grant transfer processes.
gen_risks.evidence: ...ensure they do not have a gap in provision after the closure of the NSBP in July 2026.

gen_risks.description: School leaders may be reluctant to participate in rollout cohorts due to administrative burdens or concerns over delivery complexity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Simplify funding structures, provide £1,000 upfront start-up grants, and offer first-line support materials to minimize friction.
gen_risks.evidence: ...potentially increase willingness to engage and join the programme.

gen_risks.description: Delays or reductions in budget approvals from HM Treasury for future years could destabilize national rollout expansion beyond Year 1.
gen_risks.mitigation: Submit robust business case updates early, supported by early adopter and Year 1 evaluation findings, to secure timely settlement approvals.
gen_risks.evidence: The programme's success depends on several factors. These include timely approval and budget confirmation from HM Treasury...

gen_risks.description: Shortages of qualified supervisory and catering personnel across the education sector could hinder schools' ability to staff clubs safely.
gen_risks.mitigation: Issue flexible staffing model guidance to schools and coordinate with sector partners to assist in recruitment planning.
gen_risks.evidence: ...availability of skilled staff and resources, in both DfE and the education sector.

gen_risks.description: Special schools and alternative provision settings may face complex operational challenges that standard mainstream support structures do not address.
gen_risks.mitigation: Procure specialized advisers through the educational framework and maintain tailored funding rates for special settings.
gen_risks.evidence: To support schools with more complex delivery challenges, we launched a procurement process to increase the number of advisers...

gen_risks.description: Schools may fail to comply with statutory school food standards due to catering limitations or cost pressures.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide clear nutritional templates and pre-approved compliant menu options during onboarding, backed by compliance monitoring.
gen_risks.evidence: Food provided must be in line with school food standards.

gen_risks.description: Delays in commercial procurement for the call-centre pilot could lead to gaps in data collection and operational oversight.
gen_risks.mitigation: Fast-track procurement timelines and establish interim online data submission channels for participating schools.
gen_risks.evidence: We will also start commercial processes to begin a call-centre pilot to support data collection.

gen_risks.description: Relying on only one term of Early Adopter scheme findings may obscure unforeseen long-term delivery issues when scaling to 2,000 schools.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement an iterative mixed-methods evaluation plan running from 2026 to 2028 to capture emerging operational lessons.
gen_risks.evidence: ...at the point of writing, this business case had one term's worth of learning.

gen_risks.description: Uneven capacity or engagement among local authorities could lead to inconsistent implementation support across different geographic regions.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide dedicated local authority grant funding alongside clear guidance toolkits to standardize delivery expectations.
gen_risks.evidence: ...fund local authorities to support schools and the wider system to effectively deliver free breakfast clubs.

gen_risks.description: Fluctuations in daily pupil attendance could cause unpredictable funding allocations for schools under the £1 per child model.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain the guaranteed £25 daily fixed base rate and £1,000 start-up grant to ensure financial stability against variable attendance.
gen_risks.evidence: ...there will always be a level of uncertainty at an individual school level and on a day-to-day basis.

gen_risks.description: Upfront expansion costs without immediate short-term educational attainment gains could prompt value-for-money criticisms during early rollout.
gen_risks.mitigation: Highlight immediate labor-market and household savings benefits while communicating the multi-year timeline for educational attainment returns.
gen_risks.evidence: ...costs are incurred upfront while attainment benefits only materialise after at least one year.

gt_risks.description: Lower value for money compared to the 'do minimum' option in year 1, due to the shorter funding period available for the preferred option's new cohorts of schools.
Delivery risks around staffing and food costs for schools newly onboarded to the free breakfast clubs programme.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigated through early adopter (EA) scheme insights and support funding.

gt_risks.description: Uncertainty in the labour-market benefits (parental workforce participation gains) the programme is expected to deliver.
gt_risks.mitigation: Addressed through conservative assumptions in the economic modelling.
